summary: This report reviews the key features of RIP version 2 and the implementation experience gained so far, as the routing protocol criteria of RFC 1264 required before a protocol advances. It is informational and was replaced by RFC 1721.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1387 reviews the features of RIP version 2 and the implementation experience reported at the time. It describes changes such as subnet masks, route tags, next-hop addresses, authentication, and multicast; RFC 1721 later obsoleted the report.

sections.title: Purpose of the RIP-2 Analysis
sections.content: RFC 1387 documents RIP-2's key features and implementation experience as required by the Routing Protocol Criteria in RFC 1264. RFC 1388 defines the RIP-2 protocol and RFC 1389 defines its MIB. This memo is an informational report and does not specify an Internet standard.
sections.plainLanguage: This report explains what RIP-2 added and what implementation work existed. It accompanies the documents that define the protocol and its management information.

sections.title: Features Added to RIP-1
sections.content:
RIP-2 shares the basic algorithms of RIP-1 and adds routing domains, external route tags, subnet masks, next-hop addresses, authentication, and multicast. Domains let groups of routers share routing information over one physical network. Route tags can carry information acquired from another routing protocol, and subnet masks support variable subnet masks.

Next-hop addresses can identify a better next hop when multiple routing protocols are used. The described authentication mechanism uses a plain-text password, with room for more sophisticated schemes. Multicasting reduces load on hosts that do not run routing protocols.
sections.plainLanguage: RIP-2 keeps RIP-1's basic routing method and adds fields and options for subnet masks, route information, authentication, and multicast delivery.

sections.title: Implementation Experience
sections.content: At publication, the memo describes one nearly complete RIP-2 implementation, called gated, that supported several of the new features and had been tested against itself and RIP-1 implementations. Some features and the MIB were not yet fully supported. A second complete implementation was under development, but its vendor was not identified.
sections.plainLanguage: The report describes one implementation that was nearly complete and another that was under development. The first had been tested, though some parts were not finished.
